title: Healthy neural priors improve BCI decoding in patients with motor-cortex gliomas
summary: PACT used healthy neural priors to decode hand gestures from recordings of patients with gliomas. In the reported comparison, decoding accuracy improved by more than 10%, and alignment with reference motor representations increased from r=0.66 to r=0.94. The study collected intraoperative ECoG from eight participants, four with motor-cortex gliomas and four with other gliomas. This proof of concept addresses a specific clinical population; offline decoding does not establish benefit from a deployed BCI. Review covered the abstract, affiliations and selected results.
ai_technology: Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a neural decoder trained with biophysical constraints
organization: West China Hospital of Sichuan University; Sichuan University; KU Leuven; Imperial College London

evidence.tested: Offline gesture decoding on intraoperative recordings; selected results describe eight glioma participants.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: PACT is the decoding model; it uses healthy neural recordings as priors and learns to suppress pathological noise and reweight spatial attention.
